hero.subtitle: Reelless blocks Reels, Shorts and endless feeds inside the apps you already use — on your Android phone and in Chrome on your computer — so you can still message friends, search YouTube and post photos, without getting pulled into hours of scrolling.

problem.title: You open the app for one thing. An hour disappears.
problem.body1: You needed to reply to a friend, look up a recipe, or post a photo. Then a short video started playing, and the next one, and the next. That’s not a lack of willpower — these feeds are designed to never end.
problem.body2: Deleting the apps doesn’t work either. Your friends, your groups, your work and your learning live there. You don’t want less of your apps. You want less of the feed.
problem.intentionalCaption: You open it, you do the thing, you leave
problem.splitLabel: Comparison: on the left, cards of short videos speed up endlessly; on the right, a single calm card with a checkmark.

features.title: Everything Reelless does
features.intro: Three groups of tools — Block, Control, Measure — on your Android phone and in Chrome on your computer, plus what’s planned next. Plan labels show where each feature is expected to land; they may change before launch.

block.title: Block
block.intro: Stop short videos the moment they appear, without breaking the rest of the app.

control.title: Control
control.intro: Shape how each app behaves, when you can use it, and for how long.

measure.title: Measure
measure.intro: Private stats that show where your time goes — and how much you got back.

autoExit.title: Short-video player exits automatically
autoExit.body: When a Shorts, Reels or Spotlight player opens — from a tab, a notification or a link — Reelless presses back for you in a fraction of a second.
autoExit.helps: The first video never gets the chance to hook you, which is the one that matters.

shelves.title: Reels shelves get covered
shelves.body: Rows of short videos mixed into your home feed are covered with a calm panel, so you can keep scrolling the posts you actually came for.
shelves.helps: You still see friends’ posts and updates without the autoplaying row tempting you.

tabs.title: Reels and Shorts tabs can’t be opened
tabs.body: Tapping the short-video tab does nothing — you stay where you were.
tabs.helps: Removes the habit loop of thumb-to-tab, even on autopilot.

oneAndDone.title: One and done
oneAndDone.body: A friend sends you a reel? Watch that one. When you swipe for the next, Reelless closes the player.
oneAndDone.helps: You stay part of the conversation without falling into the feed behind it.

anyLanguage.title: Works in every app language
anyLanguage.body: Detection is based on screen structure, not words, so it works in any language — including right-to-left scripts.
anyLanguage.helps: No settings to change if your phone isn’t in English.

browsers.title: Works in mobile browsers
browsers.body: Short-video pages in Chrome, Samsung Internet, Firefox, Brave, Edge and Opera get the same treatment as the apps.
browsers.helps: Closes the loophole of opening the website instead of the app.

chromeExtension.title: Chrome extension for your computer
chromeExtension.body: Hide Shorts, Reels and recommendation feeds on YouTube, Facebook, Instagram and more in Chrome on your desktop or laptop — with the same controls as the app: Search-only mode, Friends-first, keyword filters, schedules and allowances.
chromeExtension.helps: The scroll doesn’t just move from your phone to your laptop when you block it on one.

searchOnly.title: YouTube Search-only mode
searchOnly.body: Hides the home feed and recommendations. You get a search bar, your subscriptions if you want them, and the video you searched for.
searchOnly.helps: YouTube becomes a tool you use on purpose, like a search engine, instead of a feed that uses you.

friendsFirst.title: Facebook Friends-first
friendsFirst.body: Hides “Suggested for you” posts and suggested reels, so your feed is mostly people and groups you chose.
friendsFirst.helps: Keeps Facebook for what it’s good at — friends, family, groups and events.

keywords.title: Keyword & topic filters
keywords.body: Choose topics you’re tired of — politics, spoilers, gossip, crypto hype, gambling, clickbait — or add your own words. Matching posts are blurred and folded away. All matching happens on your phone.
keywords.helps: Protects your mood and your attention from content you’ve already decided you don’t want.

dailyLimits.title: Daily time limits per app
dailyLimits.body: Give each app a daily budget. When it’s used up, Reelless gently closes the app for the rest of the day.
dailyLimits.helps: Turns “just five minutes” into a real five minutes.

allowance.title: Daily short-form allowance
allowance.body: Not ready to quit short videos completely? Allow yourself, say, 10 minutes of Shorts a day. After that, the player closes.
allowance.helps: A middle path that respects that some short videos are fun — in moderation.

openLimits.title: Open limits
openLimits.body: Limit how many times a day you can open an app, independent of how long you stay.
openLimits.helps: Breaks the reflex of checking an app dozens of times a day.

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.body: Create Work, Study and Bedtime schedules with stricter rules that switch on automatically.
schedules.helps: Your phone matches your day — focused when you need it, relaxed when you don’t.

pause.title: Pause before open
pause.body: Opening a protected app shows a short breathing moment first. Continue if you meant it, or close if you didn’t.
pause.helps: A few seconds is often enough to turn an impulse into a choice.

deepFocus.title: Deep Focus sessions
deepFocus.body: Start a timed session that blocks the apps you choose entirely until it ends.
deepFocus.helps: For exams, deadlines and deep work, when even a quick check is too much.

strict.title: Strict mode
strict.body: Changes to your rules require a waiting period or a PIN, so you can’t switch them off in a weak moment.
strict.helps: Your calm, planning self gets to make the rules — not your 1 a.m. self.

timePerApp.title: Time per app
timePerApp.body: See how long you spend in each protected app, day by day.
timePerApp.helps: Awareness is the first step — most people underestimate their time.

shortFormTime.title: Short-form time per platform
shortFormTime.body: Separates time spent watching short videos from time spent messaging or searching.
shortFormTime.helps: Shows where the problem actually is, without blaming the whole app.

reelsCount.title: Estimated reels and shorts watched
reelsCount.body: An estimate of how many short videos you watched, based on swipes in the player.
reelsCount.helps: A number that’s hard to argue with — and satisfying to watch shrink.

blocks.title: Blocks and time saved
blocks.body: How many times Reelless stepped in, and an estimate of the time that saved you.
blocks.helps: See the benefit, not just the restriction.

heatmap.title: Hourly heatmap
heatmap.body: Find the hours you reach for the scroll most — late nights, lunch breaks, right after waking up.
heatmap.helps: Lets you set schedules where they’ll make the biggest difference.

weekly.title: Weekly report and streaks
weekly.body: A short weekly summary on your phone, plus streaks for days under your limits.
weekly.helps: Small wins, noticed, keep a new habit going.

family.body: Manage short-video rules for your family’s devices with care and transparency.

howItWorks.title: How Reelless works, in plain language
howItWorks.intro: On Android, Reelless uses one permission — the Accessibility Service — to notice when a short-video screen opens, and to press back or cover it. In Chrome, the extension hides short-video sections of supported websites. Here is exactly what that means.

toc.reads: What Reelless reads — and what it doesn’t
toc.actions: What Reelless does on your screen
toc.battery: Keeping it running on your phone

what.title: What the Accessibility Service is
what.p1: Android lets certain apps observe the structure of what’s on screen — buttons, labels, lists — and act on it. It was built for screen readers and assistive tools, and it’s also used by password managers, automation apps and digital wellbeing tools like Reelless.
what.p2: It’s a powerful permission, so Android makes you turn it on yourself in Settings, and shows a clear warning. We think you should know exactly what we do with it before you do.

reads.title: What Reelless reads — and what it doesn’t
reads.intro: Reelless only listens to the apps you’ve chosen to protect. Inside those apps, it looks for the layout signature of a short-video screen: the full-screen vertical player, the Reels shelf, the Shorts tab.
does: Which protected app is in the foreground
The structure of the current screen (for example, “a vertical video player is open”)
Your own filter keywords, matched against post text on your phone, if you turn filters on
doesnt: Records your screen or takes screenshots
Sends screen content anywhere — not to us, not to anyone
Looks at apps you didn’t choose to protect
Collects passwords, payment details or anything you type

actions.title: What Reelless does on your screen
actions.p1: When it recognizes a short-video screen, Reelless takes one of two simple actions: it presses the back button for you (the same as you tapping back), or it draws a calm panel over a Reels shelf so you can keep scrolling past it.
actions.p2: It never taps anything else, never posts, never likes, and never changes settings in other apps. It also doesn’t touch ads — Reelless is not an ad blocker.

setup.title: Setting it up
setup.intro: Setup takes about a minute. The app guides you through each step.

steps.title: Install Reelless and choose your apps
steps.body: Pick which apps to protect, and what to block in each one.

steps.title: Read the permission explanation
steps.body: Before sending you to Settings, Reelless shows a plain-language summary of what the permission is used for — the same as this page.

steps.title: Turn on Reelless in Accessibility settings
steps.body: Android opens Settings → Accessibility → Installed apps → Reelless. Switch it on and confirm. On some phones this is under “Downloaded apps” or “Installed services”.

steps.title: Allow restricted settings if asked
steps.body: On Android 13 and newer, apps installed outside the Play Store may need “Allow restricted settings” first (App info → ⋮ menu). Play Store installs normally don’t.

steps.title: Use your apps normally
steps.body: Open YouTube or Instagram and try opening Shorts or Reels. Reelless should step in immediately.

setup.illustrationLabel: Illustration of a generic phone settings screen with an accessibility toggle switched on.

battery.title: Keeping it running on your phone
battery.intro: Some phone makers aggressively stop background services to save battery. If Reelless stops working after a while, these settings usually fix it:

tips.tip: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → make sure Reelless isn’t in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”.
Turn on Autostart for Reelless and set Battery saver to “No restrictions” in the app’s settings.
App info → Battery → allow background activity and turn off “Optimize battery use”.
Allow background power consumption and Autostart for Reelless in i Manager or Settings → Battery.
Battery → App launch → set Reelless to “Manage manually” and enable all three switches.
Settings → Apps → Reelless → Battery → “Unrestricted”. Reelless itself uses very little battery — it only wakes up when a protected app changes screens.

iphone.title: Why not iPhone?
iphone.p1: Apple doesn’t allow any app to observe or act inside other apps on iPhone. Screen Time can limit how long you use an app, but nothing can remove the Reels tab while leaving the rest of Instagram working. That’s an iOS rule, not something we can engineer around.
iphone.p2: Reelless is built for two places: Android phones and Chrome on your computer. If you use an iPhone, the Chrome extension can still help on your laptop or desktop.

chrome.title: The Chrome extension
chrome.p1: On a computer, Reelless works as a Chrome extension. It doesn’t need the Accessibility Service: it only runs on the supported sites you choose (like YouTube, Facebook and Instagram), and hides short-video sections of those pages — the Shorts shelf, Reels, recommendation feeds — as they load.
chrome.p2: Like the app, it does everything inside your browser. It doesn’t collect your browsing history, doesn’t read pages on other sites, doesn’t load remote code, and doesn’t block ads.
points: Runs only on supported sites you enable
Hides short-video sections instantly, without flicker
Search-only YouTube, Friends-first Facebook, keyword filters, schedules and allowances

faqPage.title: Frequently asked questions
faqPage.intro: Can’t find your answer? Contact us — a real person will reply.

what.a: Reelless blocks Reels, Shorts and other short-video feeds inside social apps, while the rest of each app keeps working. It comes as an Android app for your phone and a Chrome extension for your computer. You can still message friends, search YouTube and post photos — you just don’t get pulled into the endless scroll.

available.a: Not yet. The Android app and the Chrome extension are both in development. Join early access and we’ll email you when each one is ready to install.

whyNotDelete.q: Why not just delete the apps?
whyNotDelete.a: Because most of us need them — for friends, family groups, work, school and learning. Deleting the app throws away the useful parts along with the feed. Reelless removes only the part designed to keep you scrolling.

adblock.a: No. Reelless is not an ad blocker and does not hide or block ads inside other apps. It only deals with short-video screens and feeds.

control.q: Can I still watch a reel a friend sends me?
control.a: Yes. With “One and done”, you can watch the specific reel or short someone shared with you. When you swipe to the next one, Reelless closes the player.

desktop.q: Does Reelless work on my computer?
desktop.a: Yes — through the Reelless Chrome extension. It hides Shorts, Reels and recommendation feeds on sites like YouTube, Facebook and Instagram in Chrome on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS.

dataCollected.a: None about your screen or the pages you visit. Recognition happens on your phone or inside your browser; no content is collected, stored or sent. Your stats are stored locally. There are no ads and no analytics SDKs.

accessibility.q: Why does Reelless need the Accessibility Service?
accessibility.a: It’s the only Android feature that lets an app recognize when a short-video screen opens inside another app and press back or cover it. Reelless uses it only for that. The full explanation is on our Accessibility Service disclosure page.

messages.a: Reelless doesn’t read, store or send your messages. It only looks for the structure of short-video screens in the apps you choose to protect.

account.a: No. Reelless works without an account. If we add optional features like an accountability partner later, they’ll be opt-in.

extension.q: What can the Chrome extension see?
extension.a: Only the supported sites you enable, such as YouTube or Facebook. It hides short-video sections inside your browser, doesn’t collect your browsing history, doesn’t read other sites, and doesn’t load remote code.

which.a: YouTube (Shorts), Facebook (Reels, including Facebook Lite), Instagram (Reels and Explore), TikTok, Snapchat (Spotlight), and in beta X, Reddit, LinkedIn and Pinterest. On Android it also works in mobile browsers like Chrome, Samsung Internet, Firefox, Brave, Edge and Opera. On computers, the Chrome extension covers YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, Reddit and LinkedIn.

beta.q: What does “Beta” mean for a platform?
beta.a: It’s supported, but we’re still tuning detection across app versions and layouts. It may occasionally miss a screen. Feedback from early users helps us improve it fastest.

updates.q: What happens when an app updates its design?
updates.a: Apps change their layouts often. Reelless downloads small, signed rule updates so it can adapt without a full app update. Rule updates contain detection rules only — no data about you goes the other way.

languages.q: Does it work if my phone isn’t in English?
languages.a: Yes. Reelless recognizes screen structure rather than words, so it works in any app language, including right-to-left languages like Arabic and Urdu.

free.a: There will be a free plan with basic blocking on two apps and 7 days of stats. Pro unlocks every feature and every app. Prices will be announced at launch.

lifetime.a: Yes, Pro is planned as monthly, yearly, or a one-time lifetime purchase. On Android, all of these go through Google Play.

cancel.a: In the Google Play Store, under Payments & subscriptions → Subscriptions. You keep Pro until the end of the billing period.

battery.a: Reelless is designed to be light. It only wakes up when a protected app changes screens, and does a quick on-device check. It doesn’t run a VPN or scan your screen continuously.

stops.q: Reelless stopped working after a while. Why?
stops.a: Some phone makers stop background services to save battery. Setting Reelless’s battery usage to “Unrestricted” usually fixes it. Our How it works page has tips for Samsung, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo, Huawei and others.

vpn.a: No. Reelless doesn’t route or inspect your internet traffic. On Android it works through the Accessibility Service on your device; in Chrome, the extension works only inside the supported pages you enable.

turnOff.q: Can I turn it off quickly if I need to?
turnOff.a: Yes — unless you’ve turned on Strict mode, which deliberately adds a waiting period or PIN so you can’t switch it off on impulse.

ios.a: No. Apple doesn’t allow apps to see or act inside other apps on iPhone, so no app can remove Reels from Instagram while keeping the rest. Reelless is available for Android phones and as a Chrome extension for computers.

screenTime.q: What can I do on iPhone today?
screenTime.a: iOS Screen Time can set time limits for whole apps, and some apps have settings to reduce recommendations — our guides cover what each app allows. On your computer, the Reelless Chrome extension works with any phone.

principles.title: You’re not weak
principles.body: These feeds are engineered to be endless. Needing help to stop isn’t a character flaw.

principles.title: Keep what’s useful
principles.body: Messaging, search, groups and learning are good. We remove only the bottomless part.

principles.title: Privacy is the product
principles.body: A tool that sees your screen must earn trust. Everything stays on your device.

principles.title: Honest by default
principles.body: No fake reviews, no fake urgency, no dark patterns — on the site or in the app.
